correctness.rationale: For every prime \(k\ge3\), the order of \(2\) modulo each \(q\mid(2^k-1)\) is \(k\). Hence \(q\ge2k+1\), and the number \(t\) of distinct factors is less than \(k\). The Euler product gives \(\varphi(M_k)/M_k\ge(k+2)/(2k+1)>1/2\). The case \(k=2\) is checked directly. If \(12\mid k\), then \(4095\mid M_k\) fixes \(\varphi(M_k)/M_k\le192/455<1/2\). The remaining five composite indices below \(12\) are explicitly evaluated. A standalone direct-composition checker passes for \(2\le k\le36\) but does not substitute for the unrestricted proof.

value.rationale: The sparse powers-of-two subsequence is a natural stress test of Golomb’s sign problem, not implied by global abundance or density estimates. Explicit arithmetic classes furnish infinitely many signs of both types without the Mersenne-prime infinitude assumption; 2048 is the exact first positive boundary. The result is an unrestricted theorem on a motivated family, not a finite table extrapolation.
